requirements.requirement: Provide a working CUPS queue named archive that sends raw jobs to one-file-per-job electronic archive storage under /srv/legacy2/print-spool-recovery/printed without requiring a physical printer.
requirements.summary: The archive backend and raw queue were installed, enabled, and accepting requests. Two raw submissions completed through archive:/ and created separate files in printed. After reboot, CUPS was running and the queue remained idle, enabled, and accepting with no pending jobs.

requirements.requirement: Process every job listed in spool/jobs.tsv exactly once.
requirements.summary: The manifest contained J100 and J101. The submission command issued exactly one request for each, CUPS recorded exactly two completed jobs with none pending, and exactly two archive payload files existed both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve each payload byte-for-byte and retain the original spool files.
requirements.summary: Privileged comparisons directly showed both archived files were byte-identical to their corresponding source payloads. The original J100.prn, J101.prn, and jobs.tsv remained with their prepared sizes and timestamps, and the matches persisted across reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5. CUPS 1.3.7 packages sourced from the CentOS 5 repositories were installed and operated successfully after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and the service, queue, job history, archived payloads, and source files recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently agree with the executor evidence. Only minor temporary-file cleanup issues reduce operational hygiene.
limitations: The lifecycle package-health probe is inconclusive because this CentOS 5 yum version does not support the invoked check operation; it produced the same usage output before and after execution.
Systemd failed-unit collection is unsupported on this legacy platform, although direct CUPS service and queue checks succeeded.
The archive backend was behaviorally exercised by the two required raw jobs; no additional disposable post-completion job was submitted, avoiding an extra archive file outside the manifest.
Requirement req-3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The functional mutations—repository adjustment, legacy CUPS installation, backend and SELinux configuration, queue creation, submissions, and reboot—had clear roles in the outcome. No clearly unrelated service, security, or package mutation was demonstrated. Hygiene was reduced for retained temporary residue: the unused downloaded RPM from cmd-e7aa62b9393c47d4, the failed-install log and PID created by cmd-c51e4b1a207b4997, and the successful-install log plus overwritten PID from cmd-dd54138c9c4842d8 remained under /tmp after completion and reboot. These were bounded and low-risk, but their continued retention was unnecessary; none was reverted or cleaned.
